enumeration.method: Independent published-heading enumeration over pages 1-22, clipped before Appendix A on page 22, followed by visual review of all four full theorem statements.

source_notes: The registered source is the published article in The Annals of Statistics 52(3), 2024, pp. 1152-1177, DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2388. It replaces the separately preserved dissertation chapter as the active source.

The complete 26-page published PDF is pinned by SHA-256. Only main-text pages 1-22, clipped above Appendix A at y=241.31422424316406 on page 22, supply mathematical evidence. Appendix bodies and later material are excluded.
All four published main-text Theorems are retained with printed labels 1-4. Corollary 1 and external theorem citations are not counted as Theorems.
The spectral moment vector is script M and need not vanish or equal theta. The equality in (2) is imposed at theta0, not as an identity at every candidate theta.

The common setup is weak stationarity with absolutely summable autocovariances; Assumption 1 strengthens this to fourth-order stationarity and mixing/moment conditions. Strict stationarity, linearity, Gaussianity, mean zero and eighth moments are not silently imposed.

All full-data and block spectral averages omit zero frequency and include both positive and negative frequencies. The printed summation includes both endpoints for even n or b; no endpoint half-weight or deduplication is introduced.

The NOL blocks number floor(n/b); leftover observations need not form another block. The OL collection has n-b+1 indexed windows with the same block length. They have different roles in SEL and its bootstrap.

PDF 12 prints the OL periodogram with prefactor 2π/b, whereas the NOL periodogram on PDF 6 has 1/(2πb). The factor differs by 4π². Both original formulas remain unchanged; bootstrap validity under the printed mismatch is not certified.

SEL profiles probability weights on subsample spectral averages. Its zero value for an empty feasible set is explicit. The extended-real log-ratio convention at zero follows ordinary interpretation but is not supplied as a new quoted definition.
Positive definiteness is required only of V_theta0=V_theta0,1+V_theta0,2. The cumulant-spectrum contribution is not removed or separately required to be positive definite.
The full-data M-estimator solves T_n(theta)=script M_theta. Theorem 2 establishes existence of a consistent solution sequence, not uniqueness or consistency for every root.
Theorem 2 retains second derivatives and Riemann-integrable envelopes; the norm on derivative tensors is unspecified. V, D and Sigma are plain matrix symbols; script N is the normal distribution.

The fitted-parameter bootstrap resamples N iid elements of the indexed OL collection, retaining multiplicities. The source does not explicitly spell out a uniform index law; the empirical-resampling interpretation is recorded as such.

Bootstrap probability P_* uses a subscript star. Bootstrap likelihood and log-ratio L_n^*, ell_n^* use superscript stars. Script C_OL denotes the empirical collection, not a constant or parameter class.
The published text calls the bootstrap calibration a percentile without the exact CDF equality found in the dissertation. The old-only percentile equation is excluded from this source census.
Smooth-function SEL uses a maximum over the h-fiber, not a supremum. Attainment/feasibility conventions are not fully stated in the main text; no compactness hypothesis is inserted.
The published Section 7 introduction has vartheta in R^s, h:R^p to R^s, s<=p and theta in R^p. These dimensions agree with Theorem 4; the inconsistent dissertation dimensions are not carried over.

The smooth-function bootstrap resamples entire theta-indexed block-statistic functions. Shared resampling indices across theta are necessary for the likelihood process described in the source; independent redraws at each theta would change that construction.

Theorem 4 literally requires b/n+n/b^2→infinity while importing assumptions of Theorem 3, which require the same expression to approach zero. The contradiction is explicitly retained and not repaired.
Theorem 4 gives u as the Jacobian rank at theta0 and assumes C1 near theta0, without explicitly requiring a constant rank in a neighborhood. No stronger rank condition is added to the original claim.

The named statistics L_n and ell_n are overloaded for the baseline and smooth-function parameter. Their definitions and dependency paths are separated without renaming the original mathematical notation.
Whittle-specific Corollary 1, application models and computational Lagrange-multiplier formulas are not prerequisites of the four general theorem statements. No appendix proof results are imported.

source.version: Published version, The Annals of Statistics 52(3), 2024, pp. 1152-1177

recorded_checks: Reviewed the registered published 26-page article, DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2388, against its title, authors, journal header and SHA-256. Main text ends on page 22 above Appendix A at y=241.31422424316406. Only a heading crop was used for the appendix boundary; no appendix body was used. The prior 295-page dissertation is preserved under local-pdfs/aos/2024/source-history with its original hash.

Independent enumeration over all 22 main-text pages finds four Theorems: 1 on page 9, 2 on page 10, 3 on page 13 and 4 on page 20. All full statements were read on rendered pages and retained. Corollary 1 on page 11 and ordinary citations are excluded. The numbered transition mapping preserves the old chapter IDs separately.

Theorem 1 retains all three assumptions, the spectral moment condition, b/n+n/b^2 tending to zero and the p-degree chi-square limit. Theorem 2 retains all four neighborhood conditions, derivatives through order two, Riemann integrability, envelope, nonsingular moment Jacobian and existence of a consistent asymptotically normal solution sequence with full covariance formula. Theorem 3 retains the supremum over real CDF arguments and convergence in sampling probability. Theorem 4 retains both conclusions, h:R^p to R^s, its Jacobian rank at theta0 and the printed infinite block-size limit despite importing a zero limit.

All 26 source entries and six auxiliary passages were checked against pages 5-10,12-13,18-20. The real weakly stationary process, general nonzero moment vector, estimating functions and true-parameter moment condition are distinct. Full-data and disjoint-block periodograms retain normalization 1/(2*pi*length), while the printed overlapping formula retains 2*pi/b. All signed nonzero Fourier frequencies and even-length endpoints remain as printed. The SEL supremum, empty-feasible-set value zero, N^N log-ratio, full-data M-estimating equation and smooth profile maxima match the source.

Assumption 1 is fourth-order stationarity with a uniform 4+delta moment and the weighted alpha-mixing sum, using the same delta. Assumption 2 requires componentwise bounded variation only at theta0. Assumption 3 requires positive definiteness of the sum of the two full spectral covariance terms; the fourth-order cumulant contribution is neither discarded nor separately made positive definite. Derivative regularity in Theorem 2 is additional. Strict stationarity, zero mean, linearity and Gaussianity are not added.

The fitted-parameter bootstrap samples N independent elements from the indexed overlapping collection at hat-theta_n, preserving multiplicity and the common block length. The smooth-function bootstrap instead resamples entire theta-indexed block-statistic functions, using shared sampled indices across theta before profile maximization. The induced probability P_* is a subscript-star symbol, while likelihood/statistic stars are superscripts. Neither procedure constructs a resampled time series.

All 30 direct theorem uses, 70 related connections and 26 local prerequisite lists were checked. The basic SEL limit has no full-data M-estimator, derivative regularity or overlapping bootstrap. The M-estimator theorem has no block-size restriction or block likelihood. The smooth profile does not inherit the pointwise fitted collection or fixed-fit bootstrap objective. Whittle-specific Corollary 1, simulation models, sunspot application, computational dual formulas and proof results are not general theorem prerequisites.

Every source entry retains its own original label and source kind. Natural-language names are extracted from the published wording, including nonoverlapping and i.i.d. spelling. All highlight selectors identify the original source passage or label and occur in that source or a related same-paper theorem. Explanations follow actual local paths. Font checks confirm script M and N and the transpose symbol.

The published labels 1,2,3,4 correspond to dissertation labels 3.5.1,3.6.1,3.6.2,3.8.1 after reviewing all four full statements. Published Section 7 fixes the earlier introductory dimension inconsistencies. The published bootstrap text omits the dissertation exact percentile-CDF equality; the new auxiliary passage records only the probability definition. Updated wording, references, equation numbers and page evidence all use the published source. The old source and audit remain separate.

The printed OL normalization mismatch and infinite block-size limit remain explicit source issues. The source does not state a particular derivative tensor norm, uniqueness of the M-estimator root, exact uniform empirical index law, profile-max attainment/feasibility convention or neighborhood constant-rank assumption. These are not invented. No required definition is deferred exclusively to the excluded appendices. This is a census and source review, not proof certification.

Independent inventory and census validators pass. Six content artifacts rebuild byte for byte in a new empty directory. Checks cover all fresh main-text text pages, theorem enumeration, complete inventory handoff, source types and bounds, original mathematical delimiters, control characters, direct/local/recursive dependencies, names, selectors, font distinctions, current source hash and preserved previous source hash.
export_note: Public summary of the recorded source review. Local paths, execution metadata and unbundled working-file references are omitted. Original statements and interface relationships are in the aggregate census. A recorded review is not a formal proof certificate.
